name: vccurstype
description: TYPING AT A VIRTUAL CONSOLE'S `login:' PROMPT MUST NOT TAKE THE CURSOR AWAY.  On a VC the cursor sits after `login: ' as it should, and the moment you type the first character it disappears; it comes back on the `Password:' line and behaves normally afterwards.  COUNTABLE FOR THE REASON `vccursor' GIVES: the cursor is one AttrBuf cell with the inverse bit ($20) OR-ed in (Con_ShowCursor, console_char.s), so an idle console at a prompt has exactly ONE inverse cell -- and this fixture dumps VC1's AttrBuf either side of a single keystroke rather than asking a human to stare at the screen.  Option+2 selects VC1, which sits at a getty `login:' prompt from boot; the keystroke is a raw `r' (the first character of `root').  Generous settle frames on BOTH samples because a dump can race the deferred repaint -- `vccursor's header records that costing a run, and the same trap applies here.
